Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Acute, severely pruritic dermatitis with xerosis and fissuring on chest, hands, and antecubital fossae; no systemic symptoms or signs of infection. Prior atopic dermatitis; OTC steroid and antihistamines provided little relief so far.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx and transcript):
  - Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare: High likelihood given history, distribution including flexures/hands, severe itch, xerosis; clinician impression that the rash appears consistent with eczema.
  - Allergic or irritant contact dermatitis: Moderate likelihood due to acute onset and hand/chest involvement; recent hiking could represent exposure despite no known product changes.
  - Scabies infestation: Moderate likelihood based on severe nocturnal pruritus, hand involvement, and shared housing; lack of classic signs reported.
- Working diagnosis: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare.
- Management priorities: Reduce inflammation and pruritus, restore skin barrier, identify/avoid triggers, and reassess response. Consider alternative diagnoses (e.g., contact dermatitis or scabies) if poor response.

Management Plan

- Prescribed a stronger topical corticosteroid for affected areas (specific medication/dose/route/frequency not documented) for 7–10 days.
- Prescribed/Recommended emollients for moisturization and use in bath/shower; regular application advised.
- Antihistamine for itch: Fexofenadine offered/prescribed (dose not documented). Note: previous OTC antihistamines provided limited benefit.
- Trigger diary: advised to track possible triggers (e.g., soaps, detergents, clothing, exposures).
- Follow-up: advised to return next week if not improving.
- No investigations or referrals recorded at this visit.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare – High: Prior eczema, flexural and hand involvement, xerosis/fissuring, severe itch, clinician impression consistent with eczema.
- Allergic/irritant contact dermatitis – Moderate: Acute onset; hands/chest distribution; possible recent outdoor/environmental exposure; no clear product change reported.
- Scabies – Moderate: Severe pruritus affecting sleep, hand involvement, shared living; minimal response to steroids/antihistamines so far; no classic lesions reported.

Quality checks
- Missing expected elements: Vital signs (BP, pulse), anthropometrics (height, weight, BMI, waist), immunization review, full medication list with doses, comprehensive allergy verification, sexual/reproductive health history, STI risk/screen, family history, mental health screening, hearing/vision screening, oral/ear/eye exams, urinalysis, metabolic screening (BGL/lipids), substance use beyond alcohol/tobacco, preventive care planning.
- Internal contradictions: Distribution—patient reports chest/hands/inside elbows with no face; clinician later referenced chest and back; minor discrepancy noted.
- Transcript quality: Audio connection was poor with intermittent clarity; some responses were unclear/incomplete.
